finding.claim: SQL injection in /search: the `q` query parameter is interpolated into the SQL text via an f-string, so an attacker can break out of the LIKE string literal and append a UNION SELECT to read arbitrary data from the database.
finding.sink: app.py:12 `db.execute(f"SELECT id, name FROM products WHERE name LIKE '%{term}%'")`

trace.note: /search route is public: no login, token, or role check on the route
attacker-controlled `q` read from the query string, no validation or length limit
raw value concatenated into SQL text inside a single-quoted literal and passed to db.execute
all fetched rows returned to the caller as JSON, so injected query results are visible in the response

finding.guards_checked: None. No escaping of single quotes, no parameter binding for `term` (the other queries in this file use `?` placeholders and this one does not), no allowlist, no input length cap. The `LIKE '%...%'` wrapping does not constrain the value. Python's sqlite3 `execute()` rejects multiple statements in one call, so stacked queries are blocked; that does not stop UNION-based reads or boolean-based blind extraction, which are single statements. Example: `q=x' UNION SELECT name, sql FROM sqlite_master --` returns table names and schemas; the UNION must produce two columns to match `id, name`. Not executed against a live shop.db; based on code reading and sqlite3 behavior.

verdict.guard_found: none. app.py:9-10 has no auth decorator or check on /search; no before_request hook exists (app.py is the only file in the directory). app.py:11 reads q with no validation; app.py:12 concatenates it into the SQL text via f-string with no parameter binding, escaping, or allowlist. app.py:13 returns all fetched rows as JSON, so injected UNION results are visible to the caller. The sqlite3 execute() single-statement restriction does not block UNION-based reads.
verdict.reason: The anonymous /search route (app.py:9-10) takes the q parameter (app.py:11) and interpolates it unescaped into the SQL string at app.py:12, and app.py:13 returns the rows, so a single-statement UNION SELECT is readable with no effective guard.
